title: Ralph structured review result (ralph-review/v1)
description: The machine-readable result of one Negotiation Round, emitted by a Review Agent and validated by the trusted Ralph-side wrapper before anything is rendered as a GitHub review. A payload that does not validate is refused, never repaired: the wrapper is the gate that keeps malformed or hallucinated output off a pull request. Blocking is declared per finding and is never inferred; see docs/review-contract.md.

contract.description: Contract version. A reader that does not know this exact string refuses the payload rather than guessing at its shape.

verdict.description: The review outcome, rendered as the corresponding GitHub review. request_changes carries at least one blocking finding; approve and comment carry none.

head.description: The exact 40-character commit the review judged. A result whose head is no longer current is discarded rather than posted.

model.description: The exact model identity that reviewed, as recorded on the Story's model:review: label. Not a profile key: keys are configuration-local, identities are what make an audit trail reproducible.

round.description: Which Negotiation Round produced this result, counting from 1.

summary.description: Prose for the pull-request review body: what was reviewed and why the verdict follows.

findings.description: Every objection the review raises, blocking or not. An empty list is a review with nothing to say.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the result. Fixes and disputes cite it across commits and rounds.

blocking.description: Whether this finding blocks the pull request. Required and explicit: neither value is a default, so a reviewer that omits it has not classified the finding.

category.description: Why the finding is blocking, or why it is not. The first six categories are the only blocking reasons; the last three are always non-blocking.

evidence.description: What in the diff, the checkout, or the checks supports the claim. Assertion without evidence is what this field exists to prevent.

requirement.description: The acceptance criterion, documented rule, or decision the claim is measured against — or an explicit statement that there is none, which is only acceptable for a non-blocking finding.

verification.description: How the Implementation Agent can check the claim for itself: the test to run, the input to try, the caller to inspect.

location.description: Where the finding applies, when it applies to changed lines. Omitted for a cross-cutting finding, which is rendered in the review body instead of an inline thread.

path.description: Repository-relative path of a file the reviewed diff touched.

line.description: First line of the range, numbered on the new side of the diff.

end_line.description: Last line of the range, at or after line. Omitted for a single-line finding.
